{{Short description|Extinct Austronesian language of Kalimantan, Indonesia}} {{Infobox language | name = Ampanang | nativename = ''Behasa Ampanang'' | states = [[Indonesia]] | region = Kenohan, [[Kutai Kartanegara Regency]], [[East Kalimantan]] | speakers = | date = | ref = e16 | familycolor = Austronesian | fam2 = [[Malayo-Polynesian languages|Malayo-Polynesian]] | fam3 = [[Mahakam languages|Mahakam]] | iso3 = apg | glotto = ampa1239 | glottorefname = Ampanang | extinct = after 1981 }} '''Ampanang''' is an extinct [[Austronesian languages|Austronesian language]] spoken at the village of Ampanang (no longer exists today), at the Kahala river (flowing into [[Lake Semayang]] and eventually the [[Mahakam River|Mahakam]]), modern-day [[East Kalimantan]]. It is closely related to [[Tunjung language|Tunjung]], forming the [[Mahakam languages]].{{cite thesis|title=The Languages of Borneo: A Comprehensive Classification|first=Alexander D.|last=Smith|year=2017|publisher=[[University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa]]}} This language has extremely little documentation, and is only known from a 19-word vocabulary list on ''Beschrijving van de Onderafdeeling Koetei'' (1905).{{cite journal|url=https://brill.com/view/journals/bki/58/1/article-p575_23.xml?language=en&srsltid=AfmBOorGxmK2gctqdFSAj8e1U-KaMLivcJqD-k1arW2btBb6AhHXJX2J|first=S. C.|last=Knappert|year=1905|title=Beschrijving van de Onderafdeeling Koetei|journal=[[Bijdragen tot de Taal-, Land- en Volkenkunde]]|page=615–6}} However, the 16th edition of the ''[[Ethnologue]]'' reported 30,000 speakers as of 1981. == Vocabulary == As previously mentioned above, Ampanang is a poorly attested language that only known from a list of 19 words plus its native name, and both were included on S. C. Knappert's work ''Beschrijving van de Onderafdeeling Koetei'' from 1905. While the paper largely focused on the Subdistrict of Kutai and its history, he reported that Ampanang had been already displaced by, or mixed with [[Kutainese language|Kutainese]] or [[Malay language|Malay]] among the younger generation.
